method: textual entailment only; quotes judged exactly as supplied in the ask; estate not re-read (byte-check of quotes deferred to tier 2)

rows.claim: X's automation rules require prior written and explicit X approval before deploying or operating any AI reply bot, so an @mention-summoned grokbot auto-replier cannot be lawfully stood up just by connecting a developer account.
rows.quote: Scout doctrine already holds bookmark-only; field automation rules agree.
rows.reason: The quote is about scout doctrine holding bookmark-only, with a vague 'field automation rules agree'. It nowhere states that X's automation rules require prior written and explicit approval to deploy or operate AI reply bots, nor anything about @mention-summoned auto-repliers or developer accounts. The claim's operative approval requirement is not derivable from this text.

rows.claim: Whatever courts say about public-data scraping, X's working enforcement instrument is account bans and rate limits, and the estate's X lane is the operator's paid Premium+ account, so every automation experiment prices a ban of that account and its trained graph.
rows.quote: Losing the deck to a ban costs £47/mo plus the trained graph.
rows.reason: The quote prices only the loss of 'the deck' to a ban (£47/mo plus the trained graph). It does not state that account bans and rate limits are X's working enforcement instrument, says nothing about courts or public-data-scraping rulings, and never identifies the account as the operator's paid Premium+ lane. Only the ban-cost tail of this multi-part claim is touched; the leading factual assertions are not entailed.

rows.claim: The defensible zone on X is public data read through a real logged-in session at human pace; bulk daemon scraping stays ToS-prohibited regardless of how courts rule on public-data scraping.
rows.quote: public data via a real logged-in session is the defensible zone; bulk daemon scraping is ToS-prohibited regardless of court outcomes.
rows.reason: The quote restates both conjuncts of the claim: the defensible zone is public data via a real logged-in session, and bulk daemon scraping is ToS-prohibited regardless of court outcomes. The claim's 'at human pace' is an elaboration not present in the quote, but the claim's substance is entailed by the quote as written.

rows.claim: The Grok Bot program's own documentation admits all bots share one cloud computer including logins and browser sessions and that bots are not a security boundary, so estate credentials must never ride the Grok Bot surface.
rows.quote: All of your Bots share one cloud computer, including logins and browser sessions... docs say Bots are not a security boundary
rows.reason: The quote states both documented facts verbatim: bots share one cloud computer including logins and browser sessions, and docs say bots are not a security boundary. The 'so estate credentials must never ride the Grok Bot surface' tail is the direct policy consequence of those admitted facts, so the quote entails the claim's substance.

rows.claim: The estate's rib law bars typing into native ChatGPT/Grok windows; operator paste or a sanctioned channel is the only transport, so driving a grokbot by typing inside the app is already forbidden estate law.
rows.quote: Do not type native ChatGPT/Grok windows. Mount party_subchain before speaking.
rows.reason: The quote is the rule itself: 'Do not type native ChatGPT/Grok windows' entails the bar on typing into native ChatGPT/Grok windows, and hence that driving a grokbot by typing inside the app is forbidden; 'Mount party_subchain before speaking' names the sanctioned transport. The 'operator paste or a sanctioned channel is the only transport' phrasing is partly elaborated beyond the quote, but the operative prohibition is entailed.
